author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human. The bead asks for six design decisions (D1-D6) whose chosen answers propagate into the main draft (fig9.2), the WSS/SSE handling, and the push draft (fig9.4). The author already flagged D5 as 'NEEDS DISCUSSION'. Even where the author wrote recommendations (D1-D4 and D6), several are non-trivially balanced design tradeoffs that an autonomous loop should not lock in without explicit human sign-off, because:

- They are foundational data-shape choices, not surgical edits.
- They affect three downstream implementation beads simultaneously.
- D3 (umbrella vs per-scope permission vocabulary) is a deployment-policy tradeoff that interacts with c93e545/2fd3cf7-style impl-defined authorization — the 'right' answer depends on Mark's intent for that surface area.
- D5 (suppression preferences) is explicit-author-flagged.

My analysis for the human (recommendations endorsed are tentative, not authoritative):

D1 — Wire format. Author recommends Path A (extend Mention type). Looks safe; there are no existing implementations to break. Endorse Path A as the natural extension; the optional 'id' field reads cleanly.

D2 — Rich-body span. Author recommends extending the existing 'mention' span with a scope field. Endorse; parallel to D1's structural choice.

D3 — Permission model. **This one needs human judgment.** Umbrella mention_all is simpler but less flexible. Per-scope (mention_everyone, mention_here, mention_admins) is consistent with the closed permission vocabulary pattern, and matches how Slack-style 'channel managers' configure granular controls. With 38055ec's per-method auth latitude, the wire-vocabulary choice is locked even if deployments substitute their own enforcement. Recommend the human pick.

D4 — Resolution timing. Author recommends send-time informational + delivery-time authoritative. Endorse; matches the spec's existing 'authoritative at receiver' pattern (membership, blocked, receiveTypingIndicators are all delivery-time checks).

D5 — Suppression preferences. Author's own NEEDS DISCUSSION flag. The core question is: do broadcast mentions bypass Chat.muted for targeted recipients (Slack-style 'channel mention overrides DND'), or are they fully filtered by existing preferences? Conservative answer: bypass Chat.muted but otherwise filtered; per-scope opt-outs are a future bead. But this needs explicit alignment because it shapes the Chat-update patch keys.

D6 — Push payload. Author recommends typed 'mentionScopes' array. Endorse; this is the cleanest answer and aligns with fig9.4's planned scope. Subsumes ex4u (rich-body hasMention computation) once landed — at that point my f86f4f4 fix becomes 'one of two paths' for backwards-compat or is replaced outright.

Staging vs all-at-once (open question in the bead): I lean 'all three at once' since the cost of two more enum values (after 'everyone' lands) is trivial vs the conceptual overhead of staged backwards-compat. But the author may have a release-management reason for staging.

Forward-compat for additional scopes (e.g., '@channel-managers', '@bots'): if the chosen shape is the enum + optional id (Path A), adding a new scope is a one-line wire-format extension. If per-scope permissions (D3), adding a new scope requires a new permission name. The umbrella + typed-scope approach (D3 umbrella + D1 Path A + D6 typed array) is the most forward-compatible.

Unblocks on close: fig9.2 (main draft), fig9.3 (depends on fig9.2), fig9.4 (push draft). All three are P3, all currently waiting for this decision.
